text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Friday.

GERMANY - Bund future ends higher, despite traders expectations, having traded in a range between 99.01 and 99.74, boosted by Buba comments fuelling rate cut speculation. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.53, up 0.26 from Thursday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilts raced into the close, locking in almost a full-point gain and outperformed other key markets. Dealers said the sharp rally was a typical Friday squeeze making up for Thursday's overdone fall. Monetary meeting next week to be key domestic focus. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 110-01/32, up 23/32 from Thursday's settlement price.

FRANCE - December bond future up with Bunds as Buba members soften tone on rate outlook. PIBOR up, franc stronger. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 126.50, up 0.28 from Thursday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bonds and futures ended firmer but off highs on late profit-taking, rising in the afternoon in line with other bond markets. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 123.87, up 0.36 from Thursday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - US Treasuries make first foray into plus column after data on Sept home sales and Oct consumer sentiment. Sept home sales fell 2.9 pct to 4.02 annual rate, below 4.11 million forecast. U of Mich final Oct consumer sentiment 96.5 vs. 94.7 Sept, current conditions 106.6 Oct final v. 102.0 Sept - sources. The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 111-04/32, up 17/32 from Thursday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.81 percent.

JAPAN - The key December Japanese government bond futures contract ended a volatile Tokyo session higher, but off its all-time high for any benchmark contract of 124.68 reached during the morning. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 124.70, up 0.18 from Thursday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Early primary market activity was confined to a handful of retail-targeted offerings. Russia announced details of the roadshow for its proposed Eurobond. Presentations begin on Monday, November 11. Brazil is in London today roadshowing its planned $750 million five-year global bond.
